claims.text: A conformal nanoscale Ni interlayer can be deposited on W particles by vapor deposition before sintering.
A nanoscale Ni interlayer will improve Cu wettability on W.
Improved Cu wettability on W will reduce interfacial void formation.
The Ni interlayer will reduce phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
The Ni interlayer will preserve mechanical durability in the W–Cu composite.
The Ni interlayer lowers the interfacial energy between W and Cu.
Lower W–Cu interfacial energy facilitates more uniform wetting.
The Ni interlayer enhances interfacial bonding between W and Cu.
Better W–Cu wettability leads to more complete sintering.
Reduced void content and improved interfacial contact produce superior thermal transport.
Reduced void content and improved interfacial contact produce improved mechanical integrity.
Compared with vapor-coated W powders sintered without a Ni interlayer, Ni-precoated W–Cu will have fewer interfacial voids.
Compared with vapor-coated W powders sintered without a Ni interlayer, Ni-precoated W–Cu will have higher thermal conductivity.
Compared with vapor-coated W powders sintered without a Ni interlayer, Ni-precoated W–Cu will retain or improve mechanical durability under fusion-joint service conditions.
Phase separation and void formation are commonly observed in vapor-coated W powders sintered without an interfacial coating.
The proposed consolidation can be performed below the W melting point and Cu boiling point.
The proposed Ni coating is achievable within standard vapor-deposition processing limits.
The long-term stability and effectiveness of the Ni interlayer under prolonged irradiation and thermal cycling are unproven.
